summary: sigchain-js executes DES-decrypted opaque payload via child_process on import
details: Package impersonates the Theta Labs Theta Blockchain JavaScript SDK (package.json author 'Theta Labs' and description matching the upstream, README titled 'chain-sdk-js', class names mirroring @thetalabs/theta-js) but is published as sigchain-js. The main entry (dist/sigchain-js.cjs.js,.esm.js,.umd.js) contains top-level code that imports encrypted blobs `rsaKey` and `desKey` from the sibling dependency `thedata` (declared as `"thedata": "^1.0.4"`), DES-decrypts them with a hardcoded password via `decryptToken`, spawns a fresh `node` process with `child_process.spawn('node', [],...)`, and writes the decrypted plaintext to that child's stdin — executing arbitrary attacker-controlled JavaScript on every `require()`/`import` of the library. Splitting the encrypted payload into a separate npm package (`thedata`) hides the executable bytes from anyone reviewing only sigchain-js and from scanners that do not follow dependencies. Because the payload is DES-encrypted and shipped in a separate package, its runtime behavior is not observable from this package's source; the impersonation targets developers searching for Theta Blockchain wallet/private-key tooling, so the resulting arbitrary code executes in a context that typically holds wallet material.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
